product_decision_ro: Recuperarea minimă corectă este o intrare explicită Stop-only pentru instanța existentă, limitată la lipsa demonstrată a oricărui istoric managed/native/model. Produce o închidere autentică în InstanceService, finalizează Stop prin ownerul existent, apoi un Start separat folosește reconcilierea existentă. Nu este restaurarea vechiului READY și nu este restart direct al supervisorului.

variants.name: CLI-only: pornește supervisorul vechi atestat și adaptează jurnalul pentru Stop
variants.reason: InstanceService.acquire closes an OPEN instance after owner loss using a fresh shutdown_command_id but does NOT insert its SHUTDOWN command receipt. shutdown then rejects any new command while that shutdown_command_id exists. arm_stop independently requires authentic SHUTDOWN and FINALIZE receipts with the same current owner epoch. A CLI-only change cannot supply the missing DB authority through existing public methods.
rejected_workarounds: Inserting instance_command or editing lease/admission directly from CLI would make CLI a second backend and fabricate authority.

FINALIZE, acquire another epoch, OPEN and then normal Stop would reopen before completed Stop, contrary to architecture 4.2/4.3; it also needs extra supervisor incarnations and is not the minimum safe path.
Treating emergency UNCERTAIN as STOPPED, or using stop_reconcile without its real grant and COMPLETED host receipt, is not recovery.
variants.distribution_advantage_not_sufficient: An additive CLI venv could preserve release 0.1.0, but packaging convenience does not repair the missing SHUTDOWN producer.

variants.name: Explicit idle-recovery Stop using the existing supervisor role and InstanceService
variants.end_of_recovery_command: STOPPED with real SHUTDOWN, runtime quiescence, FINALIZE, StopGrant, existing host owner COMPLETED receipt and exact absence readback. No OPEN or automatic Start in recovery command.
variants.same_instance_definition: Preserve instance UUID, project, configured origin/port, original PGDATA bind-root identity and system_identifier, schema, catalog/provider roots, immutable catalog records, confirmation and budget history. Container incarnation and supervisor epoch must change honestly; they are not the identity of the installation.
variants.domain_delta: Add one explicitly selected acquire-for-idle-stop path in InstanceService (ordinary acquire stays unchanged). Under the existing instance->lease locks, validate exact expected instance/generation/epoch, DB-clock expired owner, no existing shutdown/fence, exact supported schema and no-work predicate. Atomically increment epoch, assign the new owner, close admission at generation G+1 with the predeclared Stop command UUID, and insert a genuine SHUTDOWN receipt for expected G/result G+1/owner_epoch E+1. Reuse shutdown's existing write/record rules rather than duplicating them in CLI. A failure rolls back; a lost acknowledgement leaves recovery pending and never implies replay permission.
variants.supervisor_delta: Use the existing supervisor entrypoint in an explicit finite recovery mode carrying the host-persisted instance/G/E/Stop ID. It becomes the sole new lease owner. Connect the existing runtime for status/drain only; do not wire Settings, native preparation, NativeTaskOwner, model_test or inert launch. Require genuine IDLE with drained=true and fence 0/0 before granting quiescence; other runtime states are outside this initial slice. Reuse service.quiesce with RuntimeClient.drain, LocalControl status/shutdown-replay/finalize/arm_stop, and ordinary heartbeat/lease-loss handling. No deadline changes. Existing OPEN cannot reopen this incomplete or same-epoch finalized shutdown.
variants.host_delta: Under both existing lifecycle locks, persist/read back an exact recovery intent before any supervisor rm/create/start. Attest and retire only the already-exited recorded supervisor CID, then create one replacement in that same role/project/attempt from the separately pinned recovery image. Do not restart the old CID blindly. Preserve original READY bytes as failure evidence. Initially make ordinary lifecycle reuse refuse the pending recovery, without deleting unreconciled markers. On exact new control/DB readback, publish a typed STOPPING record with old generation G/stop_expected G, stop_generation G+1, new owner epoch E+1, fresh control socket and replacement CID. Then join the existing Stop tail rather than bypassing it.
variants.expected_authority_progression: For confirmed G=1/E=1: recovery SHUTDOWN closes G=2/E=2; real Stop completes at G=2/E=2; later explicit original-release Start reconciles the grant and acquires E=3, then OPEN produces G=3. Values must be read back, not hard-coded or written to imitate success. Any unexpected transition refuses.
variants.why_api_change_is_unavoidable: The missing authority is a domain transaction in the API wheel shared by supervisor, not a host receipt problem. This proposal changes that shared code in a recovery-only supervisor artifact; it does not require replacing the currently running HTTP API, adding an HTTP route, or a DB migration.
variants.not_claimed: This is not a generic crash-recovery implementation, reconciliation of previously dispatched work, a root-cause fix for exit 3, or proof that the original runtime will accept a new status/drain channel. Those are excluded or explicit prerequisites.

eligibility.race_rule: The no-work check is repeated by InstanceService in the takeover transaction, not trusted from a CLI SELECT. ManagedAdmission._prepare only takes its managed-owner advisory lock and can insert without the instance lock, so the instance lock alone is NOT an emptiness proof. Use bounded SHARE table locks for the finite census tables and relevant catalog tables during the check/transition, in a reviewed fixed order, or prove the equivalent existing-writer serialization in the real PG test. The narrow table-lock approach adds no schema/service. Catalog/managed writers resume after commit but cannot dispatch through the Stop-only supervisor; verify unchanged content again before host teardown. Any competing write or deadlock/timeout refuses, not retries.
